capture.final_message:
Use the `SetLike` representation of submonoids throughout. All four component statements are consequences of their carriers.

- `Submonoid.mk s h_one` has exactly the carrier of `s`; hence both the membership equivalence and the equality of coerced sets are definitional consequences of the constructor.
- Equality of submonoids is extensional: pointwise equivalence of membership gives equality via `SetLike.ext`.
- For `Nontrivial (Submonoid M) ↔ Nontrivial M`, use the trivial submonoid `{1}` and the top submonoid. If `M` contains some `x ≠ 1`, these submonoids differ. Conversely, distinct submonoids have different carriers, so some `x` belongs to one but not the other; since every submonoid contains `1`, necessarily `x ≠ 1`, making `M` nontrivial.

Thus establish each side of both displayed `Iff`s independently, then assemble the two equivalences and their conjunction. The essential assumption is `MulOneClass`: it makes `{1}` multiplication-closed and ensures every submonoid contains `1`.
